messages:
Maria (marketing): Hey runtime team — quick ask before next Tuesday's webinar. We need a small "throughput pulse" run for the slide deck: cold vs warm, p50/p95, tokens/sec, and a low-cost quantized variant comparison. Nothing huge — 3 cohorts total. Can you help with methodology + a short rerun if anything looks off? :eyes:

Ira (eng-runtime): Sure. Can you list the exact model variants, sample payloads, and target concurrency? Also confirm whether warmup should use prefix caching or the 10-request burst profile we used last month.

Maria (marketing): Model variants: mosaic-30B-q4 and mosaic-30B-int8 (quantized). Baseline: mosaic-30B-fp16. Cohorts: 1) short chat (20–80 tokens), 2) long context (2k tokens warmup + 512 query), 3) embed-ish single-sentence (50 tokens). Target concurrency: 16 concurrent clients, 100 req/sec sustained for 90s per cohort. Warmup: use prefix/KV cache warmup (same approach as previous launch). Sample payloads attached below.

Maria (marketing): ```json
{
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the attached policy in two bullet points."}],
  "max_new_tokens": 256,
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```

Tony (eng-runtime): Got it. We'll run the three cohorts against the three variants. Quick clarifying Qs: do you want cold-start measured from a fully idle node (cold VM + cold model) or just cold cache (model loaded but no KV/prefix warmed)? Cold VM runs add a lot of noise.

Maria (marketing): Measure both if easy, but prioritize cold-cache (model loaded) for slide consistency. If cold-VM is noisy, note that in the artifact.

Ira (eng-runtime): Noted. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, failure rate, and estimated cost-per-1M tokens (using current pricing). We'll push raw traces + summarized CSVs to the artifacts bucket and add a short README describing test parameters. ETA: first pass in ~6 hours, full rerun (if anomalies) by EOD.

Samuel (marketing): Please flag any throughput regressions >10% vs baseline and any upticks in tail latency >20%. We need clear callouts for the slide. Also include a single-sentence recommendation (e.g., "use q4 for 2x cost savings at <10% latency delta") if the numbers support it. :thumbsup:

runtime-ci-bot: Scheduled throughput-pulse job #3188880001 -> running on pool:dedicated-3 (models: mosaic-30B-fp16,mosaic-30B-q4,mosaic-30B-int8). Artifacts: pending.

Tony (eng-runtime): Running warmup now with prefix cache for long-context cohort. Commands used: ```bash
ci/run_throughput.sh --model mosaic-30B-q4 --cohort long-context --concurrency 16 --rps 100 --duration 90 
```

Ira (eng-runtime): Quick note on methodology in case marketing wants to paste into docs: 1) 90s steady-state window, discard first 15s for warmup; 2) measure tokens/sec over steady-state; 3) cold-cache = model loaded but server op cache cleared; 4) cold-VM = fresh instance boot + load. We'll annotate artifacts accordingly.

Tony (eng-runtime): First-pass results (short chat cohort, warm-cache): mosaic-30B-fp16 p95=180ms, tokens/sec=620; q4 p95=200ms, tokens/sec=700; int8 p95=230ms, tokens/sec=920. Raw CSV uploaded to gs://redwood-benchmarks/3188880001/short-chat/

Maria (marketing): Awesome — can you also include a tiny sample of the raw request/response (anonymized) so I can show a minimal repro in the slide notes?

Ira (eng-runtime): Yep will include one example per cohort with headers scrubbed. Also linking the summary CSV + a one-paragraph interpretation in the bucket. If anything looks off we'll re-run specific combos (e.g., int8 long-context showed a tiny error spike previously).

runtime-ci-bot: Job #3188880001 stage=summary uploaded artifacts to gs://redwood-benchmarks/3188880001/summary.json

Maria (marketing): Perfect. Can you ping here when the final artifacts/README are ready? We'll take that and draft two slides + speaker note one-liner.

Tony (eng-runtime): Will do. Expect final artifacts + short recommendation note in ~5 hours.

Samuel (marketing): If possible, include a short bullet that mentions "controlled microbench" methodology and a link to the artifacts for auditors. Keeps the claims defensible.

Ira (eng-runtime): Agreed. We'll include a short methodology blurb and the exact run commands in the README.

Maria (marketing): Thanks team — hugely helpful. Please call out any anomalies (failures, unstable tail) so we can decide whether to postpone a slide claim. :pray:
